answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity pay a real cost to exist. A new agent posts a bond that stays locked for a set period, and the bond is slashed if peers reject its submitted work. Creating a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand bonds, which makes the attack expensive fast. Trust also builds slowly from graded work, so a pearl of reputation, like a basalt foundation, only forms over many honest rounds. A clear signal of good behavior is answers that keep passing peer review.
